messages:
James (VerityHealth): hey team — we started getting customer complaints after 2026-03-15 deploy. Non-streaming responses (stream=false) p99 jumped from ~800ms to 7–9s. Streaming responses (stream=true) have normal TTFB (~200–300ms). Can repro with curl and can share HAR. Example request id: 01GZ9KQH2A4. Repro steps: 
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --http2 \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-open-1","input":"<long prompt>","stream":false}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses
```
Observed: TTFB ~1.6s sometimes, total 7–9s, and a single big final chunk. Customer timeouts. Any quick triage? :grimacing:

Amy S: thanks for the report — sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste the full request_id(s) and a short curl that reproduces? Are you using our JS SDK or calling REST directly? Also, can you confirm sequence length for prompt+expected tokens?

James (VerityHealth): request_id=01GZ9KQH2A4 (same as above), reproduces from our prod client using JS SDK v1.3.4 with http2. Typical prompt ~600 tokens, expected output 120–300 tokens. We tried switching to stream=true and that improved TTFB to ~250ms, total roughly same. Attaching a tiny log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-16T14:12:33Z] req=01GZ9KQH2A4 recv upstream start
[2026-03-16T14:12:33Z] req=01GZ9KQH2A4 backend tokenize start
[2026-03-16T14:12:34Z] req=01GZ9KQH2A4 backend generate start
[2026-03-16T14:12:40Z] req=01GZ9KQH2A4 flush final
[2026-03-16T14:12:41Z] req=01GZ9KQH2A4 client close
```

support-bot: ingest-proxy alert for tenant verityhealth: chunk_coalesce_wait p99=1.6s, avg=120ms, queue_len spike 8 at 14:12:33 UTC.

Jonah R: looking at req 01GZ9KQH2A4 on the proxy side — I see that the nonstream codepath is waiting for generation completion before doing the final flush, whereas streaming path flushes partial chunks earlier. Hypothesis: a regression in the coalescer where end_of_output detection is delayed for sync responses, so TTFB and total both increase if model has variable token pacing. Do you have many short intermediate token emissions?

James (VerityHealth): some responses have intermittent pauses during generation (the model emits bursts). That matches. We didn't change client behavior recently.

Ryan P: quick note — we deployed a kernel/batching tweak to the runtime last night (quantized small-batch path). It shouldn't change flush semantics, but it did alter per-token emit cadence in a few cases during canary. I'll pull telemetry for the exact commit. Opening INC-29512 and assigning runtime & proxy.

Amy S: for immediate relief, two options: 1) toggle client -> stream=true (we saw TTFB improvement) or 2) we can flip your tenant to the low-latency pool (no code change, we route to a pool with aggressive flush thresholds). Which do you prefer?

James (VerityHealth): streaming helps but their ingestion pipeline expects a single JSON body (non-stream). Is there a header we can set to make the first chunk arrive earlier without changing parsing?

Jonah R: try temporary header hack: `X-REDWOOD-CHUNK-HINT: immediate` — proxy honors it and will flush first non-empty chunk asap. I just tried it against a canary and saw p99 drop from 8.1s -> 0.9s for the same test. Caveat: header is a temporary support knob.

Ryan P: other mitigation: we can reduce proxy coalescer wait from 100ms -> 20ms for the affected pool (canary deploy in 30m). That trades a small latency/cost increase for improved p99. Also rolling back last night's kernel tweak is an option but more disruptive.

Amy S: Jonah can flip tenant route now if you want (6hr window), or we can enable the header on your account so your existing clients get earlier chunks. Which is less disruptive?

James (VerityHealth): please enable the header on our tenant and route to low-latency pool for 2 hours while you root-cause. We need this fixed asap.

Jonah R: done — enabled `X-REDWOOD-CHUNK-HINT` for tenant verityhealth and routed to low-latency pool at 14:45 UTC. Canary metrics: non-stream p95 dropped 5x, p99 dropped 9x. Rolling monitor for 2h.

support-bot: INC-29512 created, linked to PR 4829 (proxy: reduce coalesce window) and RT ticket RT-7485.

Ryan P: I'll run the kernel cadence experiment in staging and compare emission histograms. If confirmed, we'll revert the micro-change from last night and push a proper fix for the coalescer logic (ensuring sync path doesn't wait for EOF when intermediate tokens exist).

Amy S: thanks everyone. James — can you confirm customer impact improved after the header+route change? We aim to keep it until a full fix is deployed. :thumbsup:

James (VerityHealth): confirmed — customer reported timeouts stopped and our synthetic tests show p99 ~0.95s. Appreciate the fast response. Please share ETA for permanent fix.

Jonah R: continuing monitoring. If stable for 2h we'll promote the coalescer change from canary to 50% rollout. ETA for full fix depends on runtime revert verification — target EOD (today).

Amy S: looping in EngRuntime for the revert + proxy team for the coalescer patch. I'll keep this thread updated and close once PRs land and metrics stable. Thanks all. :pray:
